title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two parts separated by a horizontal rule.

(1) Top part. It closes a computation from the previous pages. Those pages computed equivariant Picard and unit groups of M_{0,5}, M_{0,K} under the symmetric group S_K, and contained the fibration picture M_{0,5} -> M_{0,4} = U_{0,3}. Here Grothendieck writes out explicitly two group homomorphisms ('dont la deuxième est donnée par ... et la première par ...'), each given on generators.
- (41): rho_1 <-> sigma_inf, rho_inf |-> rho^{-1}, hence rho_0 = (rho_inf rho_1)^{-1} |-> sigma_inf rho^{?} = eps_0. The rho_i are the standard loop generators of pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) or of the triangle/cartographic group (relation rho_0 rho_1 rho_inf = 1, up to his ordering convention). The sigma, tau, eps are involutions and rotations of a second presentation, presumably the extended triangle group with reflections, or PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 with S_3 acting on the cusps 0, 1, inf.
- (42): tau_0 |-> tau_inf, tau_0 (= rho_0) |-> ..., tau_inf |-> tau_inf. The second image is left blank, so the map is unfinished.
These look like comparison maps between the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} with its S_3 (or S_4) symmetry and the orbifold group of M_{0,4}/S_3, i.e. the modular-type group of the j-line. The boxing marks the 'essential' assignments.

(2) Bottom part, below the rule, is a new programme.
- Figure 1: the basic spherical triangle with vertices 0, 1, inf on the Riemann sphere, with i (or z) marked. This is the fundamental domain for the S_3 / triangle-group tiling, i.e. the barycentric triangle of the 'map' P^1 with the real line.
- Figure 2: a tetrahedron with vertices inf, 0, 1 overlaid on a pentagon, with a zigzag (a path). This suggests the cell structure of M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}: pentagons are the cells of M_{0,5}(R) (12 pentagons, dodecahedral tiling). The tetrahedron is the sphere with 4 marked points, i.e. M_{0,4} seen as a tetrahedral map.
- The list pi_{D_n}, pi_{S_4^+}, pi_{S_4}, pi_{S_5^+} names the (orbifold) fundamental groups or groupoids attached to the finite rotation groups of the sphere: dihedral, tetrahedral A_4, octahedral S_4, icosahedral A_5. Equivalently these are the spherical triangle groups (2,2,n), (2,3,3), (2,3,4), (2,3,5).
- Then pi_X for X a map ('carte'), with pi_X -> X and 'on enlève les sommets'. That is, the fundamental group(oid) of the surface of the map minus its vertices (and presumably face centres), as a quotient or subobject of the cartographic group.
- Instances follow: pi_icos, pi_dodéc, pi_tétr, pi_cube, pi_oct (Platonic maps), pi_pavages (tilings), and pi_P for P a finite combinatorial polygon.

Purpose: to build a catalogue of 'basic' genus-0 groupoids with symmetry, attached to regular maps and polygons. These serve as building blocks or test cases for the S_0 T_{g,nu} / Teichmüller groupoid project, and for the Galois action on them. This is the 'polyèdres réguliers / cartes' theme of the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: In (41), with rho_1 -> sigma_inf and rho_inf -> rho^{-1}, one gets rho_0 = (rho_inf rho_1)^{-1} -> (rho^{-1} sigma_inf)^{-1} = sigma_inf^{-1} rho. This equals sigma_inf rho only if sigma_inf is an involution. The exponent on rho in the manuscript is illegible, and if it is -1 there is a sign/order slip (unless the relation convention differs).
(42) is incomplete: the image of the middle generator tau_0 (= rho_0) is left blank.

The notation S_4^+ for the tetrahedral group (A_4) and S_5^+ for the icosahedral group (A_5) is consistent. S_4 (octahedral) is listed without '+', which is correct as the rotation group of the cube/octahedron is S_4. No error here, just ambiguity.

ideas.what: Explicit generator-level homomorphisms between two presentations of a genus-0 fundamental group (loops rho_0, rho_1, rho_inf vs involutions/rotations sigma, tau, eps), relating M_{0,4} with its symmetric-group action to the triangle/modular group

missed.claim: Grothendieck planned a catalogue of 'Platonic' groupoids pi_X (icosahedron, dodecahedron, tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, tilings, finite polygons), set alongside the Teichmüller groupoids of M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}. This suggests studying these symmetric genus-0 groupoids as objects on which Gal(Qbar/Q) or GT acts, i.e. equivariant/orbifold versions of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower for quotients P^1/G with G finite. The idea is only sketched, and the systematic 'orbifold Teichmüller groupoid' for Platonic quotients is not, to my knowledge, worked out as such in the literature. Related work exists on GT actions on orbifold/triangle groups (e.g. Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps, Collas–Maugeais).

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests GT- or Galois-action computations on orbifold Teichmüller groupoids with finite symmetry (the Platonic quotients), a line partly but not systematically developed (e.g. GT action on orbifold mapping class groups and torsion, Collas–Maugeais).

deep.surprise_reason: This is mostly a working sketch. The generator formulas are routine, and the list of Platonic and polygon groupoids reflects themes already announced in the Esquisse d'un programme. The only mildly notable point is seeing the Platonic/orbifold groupoids placed explicitly next to the Teichmüller groupoid computations of M_{0,5}, and that is barely developed.
transcription_corrections: Equation label on line 2 is (41); the first digit is overwritten but consistent with (42) below.
'dont la deuxième est donné par' should read 'dont la deuxième est donnée par'.
'on oublie les sommets' is more likely 'on enlève les sommets' (remove the vertices).
'π_pavages[?]': the handwriting reads something like 'π_parices'. 'pavages' (tilings) is the most plausible reading.
Label 'π_p[?]' at the left of the Platonic line is overwritten. The last item in that line is crossed out (possibly 'π_sphère').
The exponent in 'σ_∞ ρ^{n}' is illegible; it is probably a sign mark (ρ or ρ^{-1}), not n.
The variant label near the spherical triangle may be 'z' rather than 'i'; a separate small 'i' appears below the figure.
The final item on the last line is 'polygone combinatoire fini ...'.
